newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa penny stocks active after recommendations.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa penny stocks active after recommendations.

text.p: Shares in several South African penny stocks were active on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange on Monday after a Sunday newspaper named some as potentially tempting buys, dealers said.
Electronics firm Usko Ltd and investment trust Vestacor Ltd were the most actively traded stocks in morning dealings.

Dealers, however, said that investors should tread cautiously when dealing with these stocks, which are generally priced at below one rand each or have a market capitalisation of under 100 million rand.

"If you do your homework you can get five or six out of 10 right, you can make a lot of money. But you tend to give back a lot more than you make. A lot of the private clients get their fingers burnt," one dealer said.
The Business Times on Sunday asked brokers to list a few penny stocks they would put money in. The list included firms Vestacor, Usko and Jasco Electronics.
The paper, however, warned that since these stocks can be very volatile, they should make up only a small percentage of an individual's total investments.

Vestacor, which buys into quality companies with strong growth potential and nurtures them until they can be listed on the exchange, on Monday rose five cents to 95 cents in a volume of 1.3 million shares.
Usko, which was seen having a strong balance sheet and plans to expand into high growth, hi-tech areas, added three cents to 80 cents in a volume of 1.8 million shares.

Jasco gained 20 cents to 290 cents in a volume of nearly half a million shares helped too by news that black empowerment grouping Capital Alliance Bank Ltd (Captall) had bought a 9.1 percent stake. Jasco also said that it had reached agreement with Macmed Health Care Ltd to buy the businesses of those Jasco subsidiaries collectively known as the "scientific group".
Analysts said that the deals would leave Jasco with about 80 to 85 million rand in cash.

Engineering firm Inmins Ltd jumped 26.3 percent to 120 cents in light volume. The firm supplies consumable and capital products to the mining, industrial, petrochemical agricultural and engineering industries.
The company recently reported a 90 percent rise in interim earnings and is currently involved in negotiations which could further boost earnings.

Leisure group Cullinan Hotel and Leisure Group Ltd, which is seen having strong growth prospects and is coming off a low base, also gained three cents to 53 cents in a volume of under a million shares.
